DMK president M K Stalin on Thursday criticised the ruling TVK government over the law and order situation and alleged narcotics smuggling in Tamil Nadu, accusing Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay's administration of allowing the state to turn into a "Vice City".Reacting to the seizure of heroin worth Rs 140 crore in Chennai by the Union government's Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI), Stalin said the central agency had been carrying out major drug busts in the state every month.In a post on X, the former chief minister recalled that the DRI had busted a narcotics network worth Rs 270 crore in Nagapattinam last month, allegedly linked to a TVK functionary. He questioned why the Tamil Nadu Police had failed to detect such large-scale drug trafficking in the state."Are they unable to catch them, or are they turning a blind eye?" Stalin asked, alleging that a state once known as a leading destination for investors had now become a "favourite destination" for methamphetamine and heroin smugglers.Stalin shares 'TVK Vice City' graphic, targets Vijay governmentAccompanying his post, Stalin shared a satirical graphic titled "TVK Vice City", modelled on the cover art of the video game Grand Theft Auto: Vice City.The graphic features illustrated portraits resembling Chief Minister Vijay and a TVK functionary against a neon-lit coastal skyline, along with images of narcotics, syringes, a laboratory setup, a crime scene outline and a silhouette of a person behind bars.It also incorporates television news clippings highlighting recent controversies, including a report on the National Commission for Women seeking an explanation from the Director General of Police (DGP) and another report dated November 9, 2026, quoting a man who alleged that he was threatened into recording a video statement.Stalin also accused the state's DGP of citing crime statistics a day earlier to divert public attention from the prevailing situation.He said merely responding to incidents by stating that "a case has been registered" was insufficient, and questioned why state agencies and the 65 special task force teams formed to curb drug trafficking had failed to apprehend smugglers.The DMK chief further alleged a continuing deterioration in law and order, citing major robberies, custodial deaths and alleged misconduct by TVK cadres."With so many issues unfolding in the Home Department under Chief Minister Vijay’s control, when will he speak if not now?" Stalin asked.The development followed a DRI operation in Chennai on Thursday, during which officials seized 70 kg of heroin worth Rs 140 crore from a vehicle during a check in Madhavaram. Two persons were arrested in connection with the seizure.
Article Summary: DMK president M K Stalin criticised the ruling TVK government over the law and order situation and alleged narcotics smuggling in Tamil Nadu. He accused Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay's administration of allowing the state to turn into a "Vice City" He questioned why the Tamil Nadu Police had failed to detect such large-scale drug trafficking in the state.

Article Title: 35 yrs on, a landmark moment: Forces kill Kashmir's last active local terrorist
Article Text:
Lateef Bhat carried a Rs 15 lakh bounty

Bhat refused to surrender, was killed trying to escape

SRINAGAR/NEW DELHI: Security forces killed 22-year-old Lashkar-e-Taiba terrorist Mohammad Lateef Bhat in a shootout outside a mosque in Kulgam district early Wednesday, ending a weeklong hunt and eliminating Kashmir's last known active local terrorist, according to J&K police.The killing marked what police described as a watershed moment in Kashmir's 35-year fight against terrorism, dealing a blow to Pakistan's efforts to project terrorist violence in the Valley as a home-grown movement. It also marked a turning point in Kashmir's counterterror campaign, with police saying local recruitment into terrorist ranks had fallen to almost zero. Home minister Amit Shah hailed the operation as a coordinated success of J&K police, Army, CRPF and intelligence agencies, saying Bhat was Lashkar's last known active local terrorist in the valley.Lateef Bhat, who carried a Rs 15 lakh bounty, was killed outside a mosque in Zangalpora village after a week-long chase across south Kashmir. His associate, Nisar, a new recruit, was killed near Larnoo bypass on Nov 16.J&K Police DG Nalin Prabhat called it a milestone in the fight against three decades of terrorism, saying local recruitment had fallen to almost zero. Only two Kashmiri youths joined LeT in the past two years, he said, adding that the force was working to dismantle the terrorist ecosystem.“We have been fighting Pakistan-sponsored terrorism for the past 35 years,” Prabhat said.Lieutenant governor Manoj Sinha said only a handful of foreign terrorists remained and J&K would soon be terrorism-free.Home minister Amit Shah posted on X, “Lateef Bhat was neutralised in an operation in Kulgam in the early morning hours. One of his terrorist associates, Umar Nisar, was also neutralised in Kulgam, the day before. The entire operation was marked by a very high level of synergy. The nation salutes the brave Jawans.”Local recruitment has fluctuated sharply over the years. The number fell from 54 in 2010 to 16 in 2013 before climbing to 53 in 2014, 66 in 2015, 88 in 2016 and 126 in 2017, according to security agencies. It peaked at 196 in 2018, declined to 143 in 2019 and rose again to 174 in 2020. Of those recruited in 2020, 76 were killed and 46 arrested. In 2021, 128 local youths joined terrorist groups — 73 were killed and 16 arrested.Bhat’s killing followed a cat-and-mouse chase that began after the Nov 11 attack on a CRPF picket in Kulgam, in which three personnel were wounded. Human intelligence, CCTV footage, cyber surveillance and details from a phone Bhat had dropped while fleeing helped security forces trace him.Bhat, a resident of Khrewan Chader village in Kulgam, had been wanted for the killing of a J&K police head constable in Anantnag and two migrant workers in Kulgam in July. He had escaped a shootout in Shopian in July, when his LeT associate, Zakir Ganie, was killed.Security forces cornered the duo in Kulgam on Nov 16. Nisar was killed near Larnoo bypass, but Bhat escaped, discarding his clothes to evade the cordon. He was traced to Jamia Mosque in Zangalpora Tuesday. Police cordoned off the area around 11pm.Kulgam SSP Anayat Ali Choudhary said security forces made repeated attempts to persuade Bhat to surrender, including a video call. Mosque committee members were also sent inside to convince him to lay down his arms. “We told him that he was still young and should surrender but he refused,” Choudhary said.Bhat opened fire around 3.45am Wednesday. Choudhary said forces exercised maximum restraint because Bhat was inside a mosque in the cordoned-off area. Bhat was killed outside the religious structure while attempting to escape. Unlike earlier operations, there was little local support for him.Bhat left his home in Nov 2025, prompting his family to file a missing-person report. He was recruited into LeT and its proxy, The Resistance Front. He also allegedly operated under Kashmir Revolutionary Army, an outfit used in attempts to sustain local recruitment.CRPF chief GP Singh congratulated personnel, saying: “Some dishes are best served cold, even in cold weather.” J&K Police posted, “You can run but cannot hide.”
Article Summary: Lateef Bhat, who carried a Rs 15 lakh bounty, was killed outside a mosque in Zangalpora village after a week-long chase across south Kashmir. Home minister Amit Shah hailed the operation as a coordinated success of J&K police, Army, CRPF and intelligence agencies, saying Bhat was Lashkar's last known active local terrorist in the valley.

NEW DELHI: Maharashtra deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde on Wednesday backed party spokesperson Shaina NC amid a row over allegations that she tore a photograph of Bal Thackeray . The Shiv Sena chief clarified, saying "Balasaheb is like a deity to us" and that the torn portion of the picture showed Congress leader Mani Shankar Aiyar's face.Shinde said he had personally seen the photograph and that Shaina had already clarified the matter, news agency ANI reported."Balasaheb Thackeray is like a deity to us. Any insult to him is absolutely unacceptable. No one is permitted to do so. Shaina NC has already provided a clarification. The photograph in question shows Balasaheb Thackeray, who once took to the streets to strike Mani Shankar Aiyar with a slipper for insulting Swatantryaveer Savarkar. The part that was torn in the image was the face of Mani Shankar Aiyar. I have seen it myself," Shinde said.He added that any act of disrespect towards Balasaheb Thackeray would not be tolerated.Shinde also accused Congress leader Sonia Gandhi's memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love, of insulting Hindutva ideologue VD Savarkar. He criticised Rahul Gandhi for repeatedly targeting Savarkar and condemned those who, he said, had abandoned Bal Thackeray's ideology."In a book written by Sonia Gandhi, Swatantryaveer Savarkar has been insulted. The Shiv Sena has expressed its protest by tearing out the two offensive pages. Rahul Gandhi repeatedly defames Savarkar, a man who endured such immense suffering and hardship for his country," he said."I condemn Rahul Gandhi for deliberately insulting Savarkar, and I also condemn those who sit alongside him in government, working in close alliance with him. I denounce those who have abandoned the ideology of Balasaheb Thackeray. Anyone who insults Swatantryaveer Savarkar will face condemnation, protest and agitation," he added.A controversy erupted earlier in the day after the Shinde-led Shiv Sena protested against the distribution of Sonia Gandhi's memoir, alleging that it contained objectionable references to Savarkar.Party leaders, including Shaina NC, Sanjay Nirupam and Anand Dubey, tore pages from the book and demanded that publisher HarperCollins remove the passages on pages 201 and 443.The Congress and Shiv Sena (UBT) subsequently accused Shaina of tearing a photograph of Bal Thackeray during the press conference.Shaina rejected the allegation, claiming that the photograph was of Mani Shankar Aiyar and not Bal Thackeray.She also challenged the leaders to prove the allegation and threatened legal action over what she called defamatory claims.Congress Nana Patole, meanwhile, described the incident as "petty, low-level politics" and demanded an FIR, strict action and an apology.Uddhav Sena's Sanjay Raut said Shaina should be "publically flogged" for damaging Balasaheb's photo.
Article Summary: Eknath Shinde on Wednesday backed party spokesperson Shaina NC amid a row over allegations that she tore a photograph of Bal Thackeray. The Shiv Sena chief clarified, saying "Balasaheb is like a deity to us" and that the torn portion of the picture showed Congress leader Mani Shankar Aiyar's face. A controversy erupted earlier in the day after the Shindes protested against the distribution of Sonia Gandhi's memoir.

NEW DELHI: Lashkar-e-Taiba commander and most wanted terrorist Lateef Bhat was killed by security forces on Wednesday, hours after an encounter broke out in Jammu and Kashmir 's Kulgam district, news agency PTI reported.Bhat was trapped inside a mosque in the cordoned-off area and had refused repeated appeals to surrender, instead opening fire on security forces.The encounter began early Wednesday morning, shortly before mosques across the Valley announced morning prayers."Congratulations guys. Some dishes are best served cold, even in cold weather," DG CRPF GP Singh said.Security forces launched a cordon-and-search operation in Zangalpora village in the Devsar area of south Kashmir following specific intelligence inputs. Officials said Bhat was trapped inside the cordon and was repeatedly urged to lay down his arms.Earlier, SSP Kulgam said security forces were exercising "maximum restraint" as Bhat was firing from inside a mosque. He had said forces would take the time necessary to neutralise him while ensuring minimal damage to the religious structure.The encounter comes two days after security forces killed Umar Nisar Dar, another suspected terrorist linked to the November 11 attack on a CRPF post in Kulgam, in a gunfight near Laru bypass on Monday.Also Read| LeT commander Lateef Bhat trapped in J&K's Kulgam encounter, refuses to surrender Bhat, however, managed to escape from the encounter site.Both Bhat and Dar were suspected of carrying out the attack, which left three paramilitary personnel injured. Following Dar's killing, security forces continued search operations in the area to track down Bhat. They re-established contact with him during searches early Wednesday, triggering a fresh exchange of fire.Officials said Dar had allegedly sheltered Bhat and provided him with logistical support for nearly six months. The duo was also suspected of conducting reconnaissance before targeting the CRPF post.Kashmir Zone Police had announced the encounter on X, saying, "Encounter started with terrorists and joint party of JKP and SF in Kulgam."Dar, a former breadmaker who had been reported missing by his family, was killed a week after joining The Resistance Front (TRF), an offshoot of Pakistan-based Lashkar-e-Taiba.
Article Summary: Lashkar-e-Taiba commander and most wanted terrorist Lateef Bhat killed by security forces. Bhat was trapped inside a mosque in the cordoned-off area and had refused repeated appeals to surrender. The encounter began early Wednesday morning shortly before mosques across the Valley announced morning prayers.

Article Title: ‘Face-to-face contest’: Yogi challenges Akhilesh to contest UP polls from Ayodhya
Article Text:
Yogi challenges Akhilesh to contest UP polls from Ayodhya

Yogi Adityanath targets SP over boy's death during Akhilesh Yadav's roadshow

Akhilesh predicts BJP rout in Yogi's Gorakhpur ahead of 2027 polls

NEW DELHI: Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath on Thursday challenged Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav to contest elections against him from Ayodhya , saying he would also file his nomination from the constituency if Yadav accepted the challenge.“If you file your nomination from there, I will also file my nomination. Let there be a direct, face-to-face contest,” Adityanath said while addressing a public rally.He accused Akhilesh of lacking the courage to contest elections head-on, alleging that a weak person always strikes from behind.“He lacks the courage to fight head-on because a weak person always strikes from behind,” he said.This comes days after Akhilesh challenged Yogi to contest the polls from Ayodhya in the upcoming Assembly polls.Adityanath also targeted the Samajwadi Party over the death of a 13-year-old boy during Yadav's roadshow in Gorakhpur on Wednesday, describing the party as synonymous with hooliganism, anarchy, riots and lawlessness. He vowed strict action against those responsible for the incident.Addressing a programme in Campierganj in Gorakhpur district, the chief minister referred to the death of Aryavardhan, son of local BJP leader Onkar Singh, who was allegedly run over by an excavator during the roadshow.“What was the fault of that innocent boy, barely 13 years old?” he asked, alleging that the Samajwadi Party had made the child a victim of its roadshow.Adityanath said the boy, who was studying at a reputed school and living with his family, had been killed in a "brutal" manner. He also criticised those he accused of supporting mafia elements and hooliganism for not even expressing condolences over the death."I express my condolences over the death of this innocent boy. I am also going to meet his family this evening and express my sympathy," he said.The chief minister accused the SP of having links with mafia elements and betraying and exploiting the public. He said his government had curbed hooliganism and was preparing to take further action against those indulging in such activities."If anyone tries to indulge in mafiagiri, it will not take long to reduce that mafia to dust. The Samajwadi Party is synonymous with hooliganism, anarchy, riots, and curfews. Every mafia is their ally, and they have always betrayed the public. Just as a dog's tail can never be straightened, these goons and mafias cannot be reformed unless they are straightened out with the force of the law, and that is precisely what our government is doing. We have curbed their hooliganism, and we are preparing to tighten the noose on them once again,” he said.Adityanath said he had instructed the administration to identify those who had created disturbances on the roads and ensure they were punished.The boy's death triggered protests by his family members and BJP workers in Gorakhpur on Wednesday. Protesters blocked the Gorakhpur-Deoria road, demanding action against the excavator driver and those who had arranged the machine for the roadshow.Meanwhile, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh on Wednesday claimed that the BJP would draw a “double-zero” in Yogi Adityanath's home turf Gorakhpur if elections were held today, asserting that the response to his 20-km PDA ‘Rath Yatra’ indicated a weakening of the ruling party's stronghold ahead of the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections.Akhilesh also took a dig at the BJP's organisational appointments, pointing out that a five-term MLA, Nitin Nabin, had been made the party's national president, while seven-term Lok Sabha MP Pankaj Chaudhary was appointed its Uttar Pradesh chief.Addressing party workers and supporters during a roadshow aboard his PDA Rath, Akhilesh claimed that the BJP would lose all nine Assembly constituencies in Gorakhpur district, asserting that a united PDA (Pichhda, Dalit and Alpsankhyak) would defeat the “dominant” sections.“The enthusiasm and energy displayed by the people of Gorakhpur are remarkable. If voting takes place today, the BJP could get a double-zero here,” he said.In a subsequent post on X, Akhilesh said, “Gorakhpur is signalling that the BJP's stronghold is shaken. This time, the people of Gorakhpur will defeat the BJP in all nine seats. The united PDA will defeat the dominant sections across Gorakhpur.”The roadshow began at Gorakhpur airport and culminated at Deokahi village in Chauri Chaura. It witnessed a large turnout from all nine Assembly segments of the district and other parts of eastern Uttar Pradesh, with party workers running alongside the customised campaign bus carrying Samajwadi Party flags and raising slogans in support of Akhilesh.
Article Summary: Yogi Adityanath challenges Akhilesh Yadav to contest elections from Ayodhya. He says he would also file his nomination from the constituency if Yadav accepted the challenge. This comes days after the Samajwadi Party chief challenged Yogi to contest the polls fromAyodhya in upcoming Assembly polls.

NEW DELHI: US President Donald Trump was seen helping Chinese President Xi Jinping on an escalator at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in China's Shenzhen, in a moment captured in a video shared by the White House.The video, posted by the White House rapid response account on X, showed Trump assisting Xi as the Chinese leader stepped onto the escalator. Experts have cautioned against expecting major breakthroughs from the high-profile diplomatic engagements.

AAP-BJP face-off over defections

NEW DELHI: Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) leader Navdeep Singh Sangha joined the Bharatiya Janata Party ( BJP ) in the presence of Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini and Punjab BJP president Kewal Singh Dhillon.Sangha's induction comes amid a series of defections from the AAP ahead of the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections. Earlier this month, on November 2, three AAP MLAs, Kunwar Vijay Pratap Singh, Chetan Singh Jouramajra and Harmeet Singh Pathanmajra, joined the BJP.Several other local leaders also joined the saffron party. Those named during the event included. Vijay Tiwari, identified as a former block president, and Naresh Sharma, described as a former president, were also mentioned. (Loosely translated)The three leaders had formally joined the BJP at its headquarters in New Delhi. Their exit came after Pathanmajra and Jouramajra resigned from the AAP's primary membership, while Kunwar Vijay Pratap Singh, a suspended AAP MLA, resigned from the Punjab Assembly.Kunwar Vijay Pratap Singh represents Amritsar North, Chetan Singh Jouramajra represents Samana and Harmeet Singh Pathanmajra represents Sanour in Patiala district.Pathanmajra and Jouramajra had accused the Bhagwant Mann-led government of failing to address issues such as the drug menace, rising state debt and governance-related concerns.Jouramajra, a former Punjab minister, had criticised the government's handling of the drug problem and raised the cases of anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh Jhota, who was killed in Mansa, and Dalit man Gulzar Singh, who died by suicide in Sangrur. He had also questioned the government's failure to fulfil its promise of providing minimum support price for crops and alleged a shortage of teachers in government schools.Pathanmajra, meanwhile, accused AAP leaders from Delhi of controlling the Punjab government, claiming that state ministers did not have the authority to approve even a single file independently.Following their resignations, the AAP said it would approach the Punjab Assembly Speaker seeking cancellation of their legislative membership, alleging that the two leaders had engaged in anti-party activities. Both had been suspended by the party before quitting.The BJP's induction of the three leaders had drawn criticism from the AAP leadership. Punjab AAP president Aman Arora accused the BJP of attempting to induct leaders who had left or been expelled from other parties.AAP chief spokesperson Kuldeep Singh Dhaliwal had described the BJP as a 'kabaad di dukaan' (scrap shop), accusing it of collecting rejected political faces.Before resigning, Pathanmajra had said he would join a party that worked in the interest of Punjab.Jouramajra served in the Bhagwant Mann cabinet from January 2023 to September 2024 before being dropped during a cabinet reshuffle.The latest induction of Sangha adds to the BJP's efforts to strengthen its presence in Punjab ahead of the 2027 assembly elections.
Article Summary: Former AAP leader Navdeep Singh Sangha joins BJP ahead of Punjab assembly polls. Sangha's induction comes amid a series of defections from the AAP ahead of the 2027 Punjab Assembly elections. Three AAP MLAs, Kunwar Vijay Pratap Singh, Chetan Singh Jouramajra and Harmeet Singh Pathanmajra, joined the BJP on November 2.

Article Title: 'Not inclined to interfere': Supreme Court rejects ED plea against Azam Khan's interim bail
Article Text:
Supreme Court dismisses ED plea challenging Azam Khan's interim bail in dual PAN card case

Poll Vote & Share your view Should political figures be subjected to stricter legal scrutiny? NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Thursday dismiss ed the Enforcement Directorate's (ED) plea challenging the interim bail granted to senior Samajwadi Party leader Azam Khan in a money laundering case linked to alleged irregularities involving dual PAN cards.A bench comprising Justices MM Sundresh and PB Varale declined to interfere with the Allahabad High Court's November 17 order granting interim bail to the 78-year-old politician. The relief remains in force as proceedings in the underlying case continue before the high court."This being an interim order we are not inclined to interfere. The views of the High Court being prima facie may not have a bearing while deciding the matter finally," the bench said in its order.The Allahabad high court had granted Khan interim bail after observing that the ED had failed to supply written grounds of arrest when it took him into custody on October 31.During Thursday's hearing, Additional Solicitor General SV Raju, appearing for the ED, submitted that the high court had incorrectly recorded the facts regarding the supply of grounds of arrest to Khan.The money laundering investigation is linked to the Maulana Mohammad Ali Jauhar Trust, founded and controlled by Khan.The ED is probing alleged diversion of government funds, irregularities in land acquisition and the construction of Mohammad Ali Jauhar University, where Khan serves as honorary chancellor.The agency arrested Khan on October 31 at Rampur district jail, shortly after he secured bail in a separate case involving alleged dual PAN card irregularities.Khan subsequently challenged his arrest under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) before the Allahabad High Court. The Supreme Court had on November 5 directed that his petition challenging the arrest be transferred to the high court.The Allahabad High Court granted the ED seven days to submit a detailed counter-affidavit on the merits of the case and allowed Khan up to 10 days to file a rejoinder. The matter is scheduled for further hearing on December 10.During the proceedings before the Allahabad High Court, Khan's counsel, senior advocate Kapil Sibal, alleged that the proceedings against the Samajwadi Party leader were politically motivated ahead of next year's Uttar Pradesh assembly elections.Sibal also argued that mandatory procedures had not been followed before the ED arrested Khan.Questioning the agency's action concerning land allegedly taken from farmers, Sibal submitted that the ED's application referred to 1.552 hectares of land valued at around Rs 3.11 crore. However, he argued that the agency proceeded to attach university land and buildings allegedly worth around Rs 500 crore.Sibal further submitted that the properties had already been restored to the farmers by the district administration and that some had subsequently been sold to third parties.Appearing for the ED, senior advocate SB Raju maintained that the agency had followed all prescribed procedures and alleged that Khan had not cooperated with the investigation. The agency also presented a video before the high court in support of its submissions.During an earlier hearing, the high court had asked the ED to clarify through an affidavit whether the grounds of arrest had been served on Khan when he was taken into custody.The Supreme Court's dismissal of the ED's plea leaves Khan's interim bail intact. The Allahabad High Court will continue hearing the matter, with the next hearing scheduled for December 10.

Article Title: Madras HC stay puts NEET-PG Round 2 result on hold, candidates await clarity

This led to a dispute over which authority was competent to conduct counselling for the college.The official said the issue could be resolved within a day or two if the court provides clarity, allowing the counselling process to move forward.The court has asked the parties to seek clarification from its Division Bench on the authority competent to conduct counselling. Article Title: Bhakra canal bridge collapses on Patiala-Sangrur bypass; 2 trucks trapped, drivers hurt
Article Text:

PATIALA: A portion of an iron truss bridge over the Bhakra canal near Pasiana village on the Patiala-Sangrur bypass (NH-7) collapsed early Thursday morning, trapping two loaded trailers in the damaged section. No casualties were reported, though both truck drivers sustained injuries and were rescued by local villagers before being shifted to a hospital.The incident occurred around 5.30am on the carriageway leading from Patiala towards Sangrur. According to police, both heavy vehicles were travelling in the same direction — from the new bus stand towards Sangrur-Bathinda — and were crossing the bridge side by side when the structure suddenly gave way.One of the two trapped trucks caught fire shortly after the collapse, triggering panic in the area. Fire brigade teams rushed to the spot and brought the blaze under control. Although the trucks got stuck in the collapsed section, they did not plunge into the canal, which flowed well below the damaged span. However, following the collapse, water from the Bhakra canal began overflowing onto parts of the damaged structure.Police completely closed the damaged carriageway and implemented traffic diversions. While the parallel carriageway from Sangrur towards Patiala remains intact, authorities have barred heavy vehicles from using it as a precaution.Station House Officer (SHO) of Pasiana police station, Sub Inspector Pavittar Singh, said, "Because the pillars broke from above, there is a risk on the other side too, so we cannot allow heavy traffic there right now." He added that heavy vehicles were being diverted through the city under the supervision of traffic personnel.Teams from the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) and the district administration reached the spot to assess the damage and initiate a technical probe. Police confirmed that no repair work was underway on the bridge at the time of the collapse.According to preliminary inputs from the Public Works Department (B&R), the collapsed span was an older iron truss bridge originally constructed by the Border Roads Organisation (BRO) in 2000 on land acquired by the B&R department. The stretch was later widened from two lanes to four lanes, with a parallel bridge built by the PWD, which remains intact."The entire road stretch, along with its records, was handed over to the NHAI in 2021, and they have been maintaining it since," said Navdeep Singh Singla, Executive Engineer (XEN), B&R Sangrur, who looked after this section. He added that the exact cause of the collapse could only be determined after a formal inspection by NHAI officials.While technical experts examine whether a sudden combined load from two parallel overloaded trucks triggered the collapse, officials, speaking on condition of anonymity, have not ruled out structural weakening caused by missing or stolen bolts from the truss bridge.NHAI site engineer Abhishek Chauhan, when asked about the possible cause of the collapse and the last structural audit, said, "We are conducting the inspection at the spot after which we will be able to share the details and reason behind the collapse."
Article Summary: A portion of an iron truss bridge over the Bhakra canal near Pasiana village on the Patiala-Sangrur bypass (NH-7) collapsed early Thursday morning. No casualties were reported, though both truck drivers sustained injuries and were rescued by local villagers.

Article Title: 'Chaos if major powers clash': Xi's warning at trilateral with Trump, Putin - who said what

US President Donald Trump on Thursday met Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin for a trilateral summit in Shenzhen on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Summit, describing the meeting as a historic occasion.“We are really making history,” Trump said. “The United States, Russia and China are uniquely positioned to discuss how to reduce the number of nuclear weapons on Earth and also to lessen the risk of those weapons being used.”Opening the trilateral meeting, Trump said the three leaders would discuss “all problems that are being discussed in the world”. He said the United States, Russia and China were “uniquely positioned” to discuss reducing nuclear weapons and limiting the risk of their use, adding that all three countries had special responsibilities.Trump also stressed the importance of engaging with leaders despite differences, saying that past leaders had too often avoided talks with their counterparts over disagreements."No peace ever forged by declining opportunities," the US president said.Xi described the meeting with Trump and Putin as being of “groundbreaking significance”. According to Chinese state media, he said healthy interactions between major countries were essential.“Healthy interactions between major countries is not optional, is a must,” Xi said.He said the three countries should jointly safeguard global peace and stability and work together to address global challenges. He also warned that the world would be in chaos if major countries fought each other, adding that the world was peaceful when major powers were in harmony."World will be in chaos if major countries fight," he said.Xi further called on the three leaders to learn from history, underlining their shared responsibility in maintaining global peace and stability."Nuclear war cannot be won and must not be fought, every effort must be made to prevent it," Xi added.Xi Jinping said that the United States should do the “right thing” on Taiwan to avoid major setbacks in Sino-American relations, according to the Chinese state news agency Xinhua.Xi added that nuclear weapons should be comprehensively banned and completely dismantled, with the ultimate aim of creating a world free of nuclear weapons.Putin said Russia, China and the United States could strengthen global stability through constructive cooperation.Speaking through a translator, he said the three countries had a joint responsibility to maintain peace and security. He also said the leaders should discuss global and regional issues, including energy security.Before the trilateral meeting, Trump held a separate bilateral meeting with Xi, marking their third substantial meeting this year. The talks lasted roughly an hour, after which the two leaders and their delegations had lunch.Trump praised his relationship with Xi and highlighted their shared interest in ensuring the continued shipment of oil through the Strait of Hormuz, which has become a key site of attacks during the Iran war.He also indicated that he would press the Chinese leader to increase purchases of American agricultural products.“I’ll be asking you to do some more for our farmers,” Trump said.Xi described relations between the United States and China as “generally stable and improved” during Trump's presidency.“The efforts you have made are there for all to see and will go down in history,” Xi said.Trump also held a separate meeting with Putin on the sidelines of the APEC Summit. It was the first time the two leaders had held talks since their discussions in Alaska last year failed to broker a deal to ease Russia's war in Ukraine.After joining Putin for the bilateral meeting, Trump described the Russian president as “my friend” and said, “Wonderful things can come out of this — or at least start.”The two leaders shook hands before their meeting, with Trump adding, “We’ve had a great relationship for many years.”The meeting lasted roughly 40 minutes.
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump met Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin for a trilateral summit in Shenzhen on the sidelines of the Asia- Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Summit. Article Title: 'Bloodshed in Karachi, Hyderabad': Why Bilawal Bhutto is opposing plan to redraw Pakistan's map
Article Text:
What is Pakistan's province-redrawing plan that has Bilawal Bhutto warning of bloodshed?

Why is Pakistan considering more provinces

Pakistan Peoples Party chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari has strongly opposed the proposal to divide Pakistan into multiple provinces, warning against any attempt to split Sindh by force.He cautioned that such a move could trigger violence and bloodshed in Karachi and Hyderabad, Pakistan-based Geo TV reported.The proposal to redraw Pakistan's political map has reportedly found support among several leaders in the country's power corridors, including army chief Asim Munir and defence minister Khawaja Asif Speaking at an event at the Karachi Press Club, Bilawal said any forced division of the province would create social divisions and push ordinary people towards violence, Geo TV reported.“If the province is divided by force, society will be divided, it will lead to enmity, ordinary people will take up arms, and the bloodshed will not be limited to a single death,” he said.The remarks come amid discussions in Pakistan about reorganising its administrative structure by dividing its four provinces into smaller units. Reports have suggested that army chief Asim Munir is considering a plan to create 12 to 15 provinces or reorganise the country into as many as 160 smaller administrative units to address governance challenges.The proposal has gained support from some senior ministers, but faces opposition from political parties, particularly over the possible division of Sindh, where the Bhutto-Zardari family and the PPP have a strong political base.Bilawal said the PPP was not opposed to creating new provinces but insisted that any such move must follow the wishes of the people and the constitutional process.“The PPP supports the creation of provinces in line with the wishes of the people, the Constitution and the law. Where we are opposing, it is over force and coercion. We do not want division through force,” he said.He also questioned suggestions that a referendum could be used to decide the issue, saying the Constitution already provided a procedure for creating new provinces.“If you are looking for an unconstitutional method, how can the PPP be with you?” he asked.Bilawal further said referendums in Pakistan's history had been used for undemocratic purposes. “It is not about a referendum, it is about intent,” he said.The proposal to increase the number of provinces from four to as many as 12 has gained momentum, with supporters arguing that smaller administrative units could improve governance and public services.Pakistan's defence minister Khawaja Asif has backed the idea, saying the country's growing population requires smaller provinces for more efficient administration.Speaking to Geo News, Asif said Pakistan could consider creating 12 provinces, provided their boundaries were based on administrative needs rather than linguistic, ethnic or political considerations.However, the proposal faces a major political challenge, with no consensus among leading parties, particularly over the possible division of Sindh.
Article Summary: Pakistan Peoples Party chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari has strongly opposed the proposal to divide Pakistan into multiple provinces. He cautioned that such a move could trigger violence and bloodshed in Karachi and Hyderabad. Reports have suggested that army chief Asim Munir is considering a plan to create 12 to 15 provinces.

Article Title: A 57-year-old Haryana woman is set to become teacher just 5 months before retirement, after 27-year legal battle over appointment letter she never received despite being asked to join govt school; HC
Article Text:
Jai Mala has faced a prolonged legal battle since 1998 over her appointment as a Sanskrit teacher.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines





CHANDIGARH: At 57, with just five months left before retirement, Jai Mala is finally set to walk into a classroom as a Sanskrit teacher, 27 years after she was asked to join a Haryana government school but never received her appointment letter.The Punjab and Haryana high court on Monday directed the Haryana government to appoint her with effect from June 10, 1999, along with all consequential benefits, setting aside the judgments of two lower courts that had rejected her claim.“Though I have only five months of service left before my scheduled retirement in April, I can’t wait to step into a classroom. This is what I have been waiting for,” Jai Mala, now 57, told TOI on Wednesday.The 27-year-long fight, however, came at a heavy personal cost. Her husband, Roop Chand, said the prolonged uncertainty and repeated disappointments took a toll on her mental and physical health. She slipped into depression and also suffered a cardiac attack, he said.“We spent lakhs of rupees, suffered disappointments, but I am happy that after 27 years of struggle, justice has prevailed,” Jai Mala said.Her ordeal began in December 1998, when she was called for an interview for the post of Sanskrit teacher.In June 1999, the district education officer scrutinised her certificates and asked her to join a government school in Rewari. However, the formal appointment letter never arrived.Despite approaching the authorities repeatedly, she failed to get the letter. She eventually filed a suit seeking appointment with effect from June 10, 1999, along with arrears of salary and allowances and interest.The Haryana government opposed her claim, arguing that she had not submitted a certificate establishing knowledge of Hindi up to the matriculation standard, a prerequisite for the post. It also disputed her contention that she had studied Hindi during her BA.The dispute centred on her educational qualifications. Jai Mala held BA and B.Ed degrees, with Sanskrit and English as subjects. She had also studied Hindi in both Part-I and Part-II of her BA.A trial court dismissed her suit on May 18, 2006. The Rewari district judge upheld the decision on October 11, 2006, forcing her to approach the high court.Before the high court, her counsel argued that the lower courts had overlooked documentary evidence showing that she had secured 106 out of 200 marks in Hindi in BA Part-I and 89 out of 200 in Part-II. Having passed Hindi at the graduation level, she possessed a qualification higher than the minimum knowledge of Hindi prescribed for the post, the counsel submitted.The state counsel maintained that the earlier judgments were based on a proper appreciation of the facts.The high court, however, found merit in Jai Mala's argument. Justice Manuja observed that the documentary evidence clearly established that she had studied Hindi during her BA.Referring to Haryana government's instructions dated June 16, 1979, and a Supreme Court judgment, the court held that a higher academic qualification in the prescribed subject could not be disregarded merely because she had not studied Hindi at the matriculation level.“Once the appellant-plaintiff acquired higher academic qualification in the very subject for which knowledge was prescribed, the mere fact that she had not studied Hindi at the matriculation level could not, by itself, have rendered her ineligible for the post,” Justice Manuja observed.The court also took note of the authorities asking her to join the school before withholding the formal appointment order.“The respondents’ conduct in asking the appellant to join and thereafter withholding the formal appointment order lends support to her case, reflecting a lack of due diligence on their part,” the bench said.With the high court ruling in her favour, Jai Mala said she was looking forward to starting work and performing her duties diligently.Her husband, who works as a computer teacher at a government college in Rewari, said their education helped them sustain the prolonged legal battle.“We could persist with this legal battle only because we are educated and understood the legal process. Otherwise, it would have been extremely difficult for an ordinary family to sustain such a long fight,” he said.
Article Summary: Jai Mala was asked to join a Haryana government school but never received her appointment letter. The dispute centred on her educational qualifications. She held BA and B.Ed degrees, with Sanskrit and English as subjects. She had also studied Hindi in both Part-I and Part-II of her BA. Her husband said the prolonged uncertainty took a toll on her mental and physical health.

Article Title: In 1970s, Dawood Ibrahim lived here with family before his rise in Mumbai's underworld; now, 87-year-old building faces demolition
Article Text:
BMC plans to commence the demolition of Haji Ismail Haji Habib Musafirkhana, which housed Dawood Ibrahim's family.

MUMBAI: The BMC is likely to begin demolishing the 87-year-old Haji Ismail Haji Habib Musafirkhana on Thursday. The building was once home to the family of underworld don Dawood Ibrahim . BMC had scheduled the demolition for Nov 18 and 19. But work did not begin on Wednesday.A civic notice said BMC received a letter from Saifee Burhani Upliftment Trust (SBUT) on the building's dilapidated and dangerous condition, requesting BMC to evict its occupants and demolish the structure in accordance with a Bombay High Court order of Aug 2020. In clarification issued on Oct 23 this year, SBUT stated the building falls under Sector 8 of its cluster redevelopment scheme, with a portion of it lying within the alignment of a proposed road.An officer said police were ready to provide protection and would proceed to the site whenever BMC called them.Constructed in 1939, the ground-plus-one-storey building has 36 rooms and was initially used as temporary accommodation for Haj pilgrims. It was later categorised as a C-1 structure, indicating it was dilapidated. A demolition notice was then issued.The civic notice stated an internal road was under construction and the C-1 structure fell within its alignment, obstructing the widening of the Second Cooper Street layout road.The occupant of the ground-floor prayer hall was asked to move to alternative accommodation offered by SBUT. During a recent site inspection, BMC found the building had been vacated, except for the ground floor (used as a prayer hall).In the early 1970s, police constable Ibrahim Kaskar, his wife Amina Bi and their children moved from Temkar Mohalla to a room in Musafirkhana.One of their children, Dawood Ibrahim, took to crime and emerged as a major threat to rival gangs. He allegedly occupied space on the ground floor, near the building's entrance, where he would sit with friends and gang members.Dawood fled Mumbai in 1986. The building had more than two dozen tenants. A lane away stood Damarwala Building, where Dawood's younger brother, Iqbal Kaskar, stayed after his release from Arthur Road Jail in 2007. Kaskar had been deported from UAE in 2003 along with a dozen other members of the Dawood gang.The SBUT, which is undertaking a cluster redevelopment project in Bhendi Bazar, acquired six rooms in Damarwala Building through a public auction conducted by the Smugglers and Foreign Exchange Manipulators (Forfeiture of Property) Act (SAFEMA) authorities.The rooms were allegedly owned by Kaskar and Dawood's relatives. Hotel Raunaq Afroz, also known as Delhi Zaika, near Damarwala Building, was also acquired by SBUT through an auction. The Shabnam Guest House, allegedly owned by Dawood's relatives and located around 2,000 metres from the Musafirkhana, was also auctioned.
Article Summary: Haji Ismail Haji Habib Musafirkhana was once home to the family of underworld don Dawood Ibrahim. BMC had scheduled the demolition for Nov 18 and 19, but work did not begin on Wednesday. A civic notice said BMC received a letter from Saifee Burhani Upliftment Trust (SBUT) on the building's dilapidated condition.

Article Title: US flight chaos continues: 2,400 flights cancelled, 8,800 delayed as recovery drags on
Article Text:
US flight chaos enters third day, over 10,000 flights hit

One router, a chain of problems: What went wrong

FAA still has no clear answer

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

US flyers had to face another day of long waits and disrupted travel on Sunday, as more than 10,000 flights remained cancelled or delayed for the third day in a row.While airlines raced to get their schedules back on track, transportation secretary Sean Duffy said that things could return to normal by Monday (local time).The disruption began after a router replacement triggered a chain of technical problems across air traffic control centres. The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) is yet to identify the exact cause, even as the incident has renewed concerns about ageing technology and the need to upgrade the country's air traffic systems.The disruption continued to affect airlines across the country on Sunday. According to aviation data site FlightAware, more than 2,300 flights were cancelled and around 7,700 delayed.Saturday was even worse, with airlines cancelling more than 6,400 flights and reporting over 8,000 delays, according to Reuters.JetBlue saw the highest cancellations on Sunday, with 28% of its flights affected. American Airlines cancelled 17% of its flights, while United Airlines, Southwest and Delta reported cancellations of 3% to 5%.Speaking on ABC, Duffy said that flights would come "back to normal" on Sunday "but probably fully normal" on Monday.He also stressed that keeping passengers safe remained the FAA's priority.The trouble started with maintenance work involving routers used by the FAA. According to officials, the installation of at least one new router by FAA contractor L3Harris at a remote facility led to a huge flow of data at other air traffic control centres, affecting their communication systems.Duffy said the replacement of a router at an FAA facility in El Dorado, Arkansas, triggered problems with a recently replaced router in Amarillo, Texas. The Amarillo router began broadcasting, causing other routers at air traffic control centres across the country to become overloaded.The FAA said on Sunday that it had disabled the "functionality of the originating routers". It also took the same step for around 60 similar routers used in the air traffic control system.However, the exact reason behind the failure remains unclear. Duffy said the maintenance work had been carried out thousands of times in the past without any problems.The worker who installed the router was not suspected of deliberately causing the disruption.The worker was "a good American patriot, we believe, a veteran — so we don't think that someone tried to sabotage the network on the install," Duffy said. "But we don't actually have the root cause."Duffy also said the routers that experienced problems were bought in 2001 and had become outdated by 2006.The technical failure led the FAA to issue a nationwide ground stop on Friday, bringing nearly all departing flights to a halt for almost five hours.It was the longest nationwide halt to US air travel since the September 11, 2001, al Qaeda attacks on the United States.Duffy said there was no evidence of a cyberattack or any other deliberate attempt to disrupt the system. However, the FAA is still trying to establish what caused the failure.The incident has once again highlighted the challenges facing the US air traffic control system. It has been struggling with ageing technology, equipment and communication problems, along with a shortage of several thousand air traffic controllers.The flight disruptions have added urgency to the debate over modernising the country's air traffic control system.Duffy has called for $50 billion in funding to upgrade the infrastructure, raising his earlier demand of $30 billion. This is in addition to the $12.5 billion approved by Congress last year.US President Donald Trump also called for more funding on Sunday, making his first public comments on the weekend's air travel disruptions."We have already started the work, but it should be done all at once, not in drips and drabs," Trump wrote on social media. "Congress must approve."But the demand for more money has not gone unchallenged. US Representatives Rick Larsen and André Carson, the top Democrats on the House of Representatives Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure and its aviation subcommittee, respectively, questioned why additional funds were needed.
Article Summary: More than 10,000 flights cancelled or delayed for third day in a row. Transportation secretary Sean Duffy said things could return to normal by Monday. The disruption began after a router replacement triggered a chain of technical problems across air traffic control centres. The Federal Aviation Administration is yet to identify the exact cause.

Article Title: Brent crude falls over $1 as Trump signals fresh US strikes on Iran are unlikely
Article Text:
Crude oil eases after Trump's remarks

Trump warns Iran despite ruling out fresh strikes

Hormuz caught in chokehold

Oil prices opened lower on Monday, with Brent crude briefly shedding more than $1 a barrel.The dip comes after US President Donald Trump said that fresh American strikes on Iran were “highly unlikely” if negotiations between the two countries made progress.Brent crude futures fell 52 cents, or 0.53%, to $97.80 a barrel. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures slipped 15 cents, or 0.17%, to $90.68 a barrel.Trump's comments offered an indication that the US could avoid another round of military action against Iran, provided Tehran agreed to what he described as a strong deal. However, reports from both countries of shipping being hit in and around the Strait of Hormuz kept concerns over disruptions to the strategic waterway alive."It depends on whether or not they sign a very strong agreement," Trump told CNN in a phone interview. "The answer is, highly unlikely it's going to be necessary."In a 20-minute telephone interview with CNN, Trump repeated five times that renewed military intervention was unlikely if Iran made tangible progress in negotiations over its nuclear programme and the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.The US president, however, warned that Washington had identified 38 Iranian bridges that could be destroyed within an hour if further military action became necessary."We have 38 bridges in our site that we can knock down in literally one hour. They’ll all be down," Trump told CNN.The remarks come amid continued disruption to crude oil supplies through the Strait of Hormuz, which has now lasted for over eight months. The disruption has affected refinery operations across major Asian and Middle Eastern economies.According to the US Energy Information Administration (EIA), global refinery activity fell sharply in the second quarter of 2026 after the Middle East conflict broke out.Data from energy intelligence firm Kpler showed that global refinery inputs dropped by 4.8 million barrels per day (b/d), or 6%, in April-June compared with the previous quarter. However, they recovered by 1.8 million b/d in the third quarter as refiners adapted to changing trade flows and alternative supply routes.Countries that rely heavily on crude supplies passing through the Strait of Hormuz were among the worst affected.China saw the biggest decline, with refinery inputs falling by 2.1 million b/d in the second quarter and a further 0.8 million b/d in the third quarter.India, South Korea and Japan together recorded a drop of more than 1 million b/d in crude oil inputs in the second quarter. Their combined inputs recovered by 0.8 million b/d in the following quarter.
Article Summary: Brent crude futures fell 52 cents, or 0.53%, to $97.80 a barrel. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures slipped 15 cents, to $90.68 a barrels. US President Donald Trump said fresh American strikes on Iran were “highly unlikely” if negotiations between the two countries made progress.

NEW DELHI: Former Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has formally sought a new passport and national identity card (NID), taking a step towards her planned return from India in December.The information comes from a Monday letter sent by Hasina’s lawyers to the acting high commissioner at Bangladesh's embassy in Delhi, Preeti Rahman, Reuters reported.Hasina's lawyers at London-based Matrix Chambers requested the issuance of fresh documents. They cited the reported cancellation of her existing passport and NID by Bangladesh's interim government and other authorities."In view of the reported revocation of her existing Bangladeshi passport and National Identity Card (NID) by the Interim Government and other authorities, I respectfully request that you take the necessary steps to issue a new Bangladeshi passport and National Identity Card for our client," the lawyers wrote.The letter urged the authorities to process the applications "expeditiously", citing Hasina's Bangladeshi nationality and the country's "obligations arising under international human rights instruments".However, Bangladesh denied Hasina’s request, stating that the country does not provide "passport to a terrorist"."She is a fugitive criminal. We have an active extradition treaty with India. We want her handed over," Bangladesh state minister for foreign affairs, Humaiun Kobir, told reporters."Should we treat her like an ordinary commercial traveller and tell her ​to come and visit her ​in-laws’ residence?" Kobir jibed.According to Reuters, the request is the clearest indication yet that Hasina is taking steps to act on her stated intention to return in December, more than two years after a deadly uprising forced her from power. Her return could reignite political and legal tensions as Bangladesh attempts to restore stability and her Awami League party remains banned.Hasina intends to return and surrender before a court. Her aides said on Monday that the date would be announced after the completion of various formalities.Last week, the exiled leader the Associated Press she would prefer dying in her own land, among her own people.“If death is my destiny, I would rather die on the soil of my own country, among my own people,” Hasina said.In November 2025, Bangladesh's war-crimes tribunal sentenced Hasina to death in absentia for ordering a crackdown on the student-led uprising. She has denied the charges, rejected the verdict and questioned the legitimacy of the trial.The crackdown killed hundreds of protesters and left thousands injured. According to United Nations data cited by the Associated Press, nearly 1,400 people were killed during the unrest.Bangladesh has repeatedly sought Hasina's extradition from India. New Delhi has said the request is being examined through legal channels.Hasina's Awami League was Bangladesh's largest political party before it was banned following her removal from office. Several of its leaders and members have since been jailed, while others have gone into self-imposed exile in India and elsewhere.Having served as Prime Minister for 20 years across multiple terms, Hasina retains support among sections of the population. Her return could deepen political divisions as the country continues to deal with the aftermath of the upheaval.It could also have implications for Bangladesh's strained relationship with India, which deteriorated sharply after New Delhi gave the former prime minister refuge.
Article Summary: Sheikh Hasina has formally sought a new passport and national identity card (NID) The request is reportedly the clearest indication yet that Hasina is taking steps to act on her stated intention to return in December. Article Title: A week of grounded flights and JPMorgan Chase, Microsoft Outlook and NSA network outages; bank CEOs, US spy agency brief Congress, officials blames AI, saying: These models are...
Article Text:
Microsoft: Our outage didn’t ground US flights (Image: AP)

AI is finding software bugs faster than companies can safely fix them

NSA network went down after a patch for PHP flaws, US intelligence chief says

Microsoft, FAA and Chase outages each had a different trigger

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A week of tech outages that grounded every flight in the US, slowed JPMorgan Chase transactions, knocked Microsoft Outlook offline for millions and took down a classified National Security Agency network may come down to one thing: a rush to fix security holes found by artificial intelligence. Wall Street executives and the NSA have told members of Congress that the disruptions were caused by attempts to patch vulnerabilities identified by AI models, The Washington Sun reported, citing three sources familiar with the private conversations.None of the outages appear to be the result of a cyberattack. Instead, officials told lawmakers that the fixes themselves temporarily overwhelmed the systems they were meant to protect."These models are identifying massive vulnerabilities, and that increases the urgency to patch right away," a congressional official briefed on the matter told the publication. "They're trying to push through a lot of patches all at once," the official added, calling it "more than the system was designed for."The logic is simple enough. Companies and government agencies have been turning powerful AI models on their own systems to find weak spots before hackers do.Once a gap shows up, the clock starts ticking, because attackers have access to similar AI tools or soon will. That pressure has pushed banks, tech firms and even the intelligence community to roll out fixes faster than they normally would, according to The Washington Sun.The scale has changed quickly. Microsoft fixed about 1,400 security flaws in a single monthly update last month, a record, The Wall Street Journal reported. A year earlier, the figure was about 170. The report tied the jump to AI models built for bug hunting, including Anthropic's Mythos, which arrived in April, and similar models from OpenAI. Serious flaws have since surfaced in PHP, the Linux operating system and the Java programming language.The NSA is the clearest example so far. Its classified internal network, NSANet, which staff use to send and receive top secret information, went offline on Tuesday. Employees were told to stagger their arrivals at the agency's Fort Meade, Maryland headquarters, The New York Times reported, adding that the network had been unstable for weeks. Publicly, the agency pointed to "scheduled routine maintenance."Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton later said the outage came from a software patch for major PHP vulnerabilities discovered last month. PHP powers about 70% of the world's websites. "This is not a cyberattack, and this is not a coordinated action by a nation state," Clayton said in a TV interview, adding that "many people are patching their systems."Not every failure this week fits neatly into the AI patching explanation. Microsoft's Outlook outage on Thursday left more than 450 million Microsoft 365 users unable to send or receive email, according to The Wall Street Journal, and took nearly 24 hours to fix. Microsoft traced it to a latent bug that had been sitting on its networking gateway servers since July.The FAA's nationwide ground stop on Friday followed a flood of data hitting its network at 1,000 connection attempts every four to five seconds. A new router at a site in El Dorado, Arkansas, is among the suspects. About 3,500 planes in the air landed safely, and airlines cancelled roughly 12,462 flights that day, according to the FAA, which blamed its legacy equipment rather than its modernisation work.On Monday, Chase said a software bug slowed transactions, with delays spilling over to other banks and Zelle payments. United Airlines and Apple also reported outages, with Apple citing "an internal update."House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries has asked the administration to brief Congress. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin, meanwhile, said that "they're pushing new technology on top of really old computer systems, and it just seems to overwhelm the system." "We're going to see more of this as new technology rolls out," Mullin said.
Article Summary: NSA network went down after a patch for PHP flaws, US intelligence chief says. Microsoft, FAA and Chase outages each had a different trigger. Wall Street executives and NSA have told members of Congress that the disruptions were caused by attempts to patch vulnerabilities identified by AI models.

Article Title: US Federal Court judge 'cancels' fixed terms of admission for F, J, and I non-immigrant visas; says that it is against Congress’s intent in creating the subject visa programs: Here's why it is good ne
Article Text:
US Federal Court judge 'cancels' fixed terms of admission for F, J, and I non-immigrant visas; says that it is against Congress’s intent in creating the subject visa programs: Here's why it is good news for international students

What was the US visa rule that the court struck down

F-1 visas: For international students pursuing academic studies in the US.

J-1 visas: For exchange visitors participating in approved exchange programmes.

I visas: For representatives of foreign information media working in the US.

Why did the US court cancel the fixed admission rule

Why is the ruling good news for international students

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

International students in the US have received a major relief (at least for the time being) after a federal court struck down a regulation that sought to introduce fixed stay limits for foreign students, exchange visitors and foreign media representatives. A federal district court in Massachusetts ruled against the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) regulation, finding that it went against Congress's intent when it created the F, J and I visa programmes. The court also found that the regulation violated the Administrative Procedure Act (APA).The decision was delivered by Judge Dennis Saylor in the case Presidents’ Alliance on Higher Education and Immigration et al. v. US Department of Homeland Security et al., filed in August 2026.The DHS regulation aimed to replace the existing duration-of-status system with fixed periods of admission for certain non-immigrant visa holders. Under the duration-of-status system, foreign students and exchange visitors can generally remain in the US as long as they continue to meet the requirements of their authorised status. The proposed regulation sought to replace this arrangement with specific time limits on their stay.The rule covered three categories of non-immigrant visas:The proposed changes also covered dependents of these visa holders.The court found that the DHS regulation exceeded the department's authority and was inconsistent with Congress's intent in creating the F, J and I visa programmes. The ruling also stated that the regulation violated the Administrative Procedure Act, which sets requirements for how federal agencies introduce and implement rules.The legal challenge was filed in August 2026 by a coalition of educational organisations and unions. The groups included NAFSA, the Presidents’ Alliance on Higher Education and Immigration, the American Federation of Teachers and the United Auto Workers (UAW).They argued that replacing duration-of-status admissions with fixed periods would violate the Administrative Procedure Act. In September, the court had temporarily postponed the regulation's effective date while the legal proceedings continued. It has now vacated the rule.The decision is significant for international students because the proposed regulation would have replaced the duration-of-status system with fixed admission periods. With the regulation vacated, the proposed fixed-term restrictions will not take effect under this rule. The existing duration-of-status framework remains in place, subject to the applicable immigration requirements.This is also relevant for exchange visitors and foreign media representatives covered by the J and I visa categories.However, the ruling may not be the final word on the matter as the Trump administration is expected to appeal the decision.
Article Summary: US Federal Court judge 'cancels' fixed terms of admission for F, J, and I non- immigrant visas; says that it is against Congress’s intent in creating the subject visa programs. With the regulation vacated, the proposed fixed-term restrictions will not take effect under this rule.

Article Title: Dadar station to be renamed Chaityabhoomi, says CM Devendra Fadnavis
Article Text:
CM Devendra Fadnavis announced the completion of a legislative process to rename Dadar railway station as Chaityabhoomi.

Govt’s plan to rename Dadar station sparks debate online

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines





MUMBAI: CM Devendra Fadnavis Wednesday announced that the legislative process to rename Dadar railway station as Chaityabhoomi would be completed during the legislature's winter session next month.Dec 6 marks the death anniversary of Dr B R Ambedkar, observed as Mahaparinirvan Din, when thousands of his followers from across the country converge at his memorial, Chaityabhoomi, in Dadar to pay homage. The CM's announcement appears to be an outreach to Dalits ahead of the occasion.Historians say the name Dadar came about as it literally means a staircase or ladder in Marathi and the locality was regarded "as part of a ladder leading to the island city".The meeting to review preparations for the occasion was attended by DCMs Eknath Shinde & Sunetra Pawar. Fadnavis said the state had written to Centre conveying its in-principle approval for the renaming of Dadar, one of Mumbai's busiest stations. "The Centre has issued guidelines regarding a legislative committee. The process will be completed," he said.Elphinstone Road station was renamed Prabhadevi a few years ago.The state govt’s decision to rename Dadar railway station as Chaityabhoomi sparked a debate on social media, with some terming it Dalit appeasement, and others pointing out that it tampers with the historical identity of the area.In 2023, city Congress president and North-Central Mumbai MP Varsha Gaikwad had demanded that Dadar station be renamed Chaityabhoomi, pointing out that Elphinstone Road station had been renamed Prabhadevi and the new Oshiwara station Ram Mandir, despite the much older demand for Dadar. Avinash Mhatekar of RPI (A) said the demand dated back to immediately after Ambedkar's death and accused Railways of delaying it. "We welcome the govt’s decision," he said. AICC national secretary Sachin Sawant questioned the delay, alleging political motives: "The govt must explain the delay. It renamed Prabhadevi, so it knows the procedure. It must also explain the delay in constructing Ambedkar memorial at Indu Mills.”The CM said most work on the Indu Mills memorial was complete, with some issues about the main statue remaining. A meeting will be held next week to resolve them. For Mahaparinirvan Din, he directed the home department to ban demonstrations, protests and morchas near Chaityabhoomi. "The police and administration must pay special attention to ensuring a disciplined and sombre atmosphere around Chaityabhoomi," he said.He also directed the traffic department and police to coordinate to ensure smooth movement of visitors to and from the memorial.All statues of Dr Ambedkar across the state will be cleaned and spruced up ahead of the occasion. Fadnavis directed officials to clear all hurdles and implement the decision within a week.
Article Summary: Dec 6 marks the death anniversary of Dr B R Ambedkar, observed as Mahaparinirvan Din. Thousands of his followers from across the country converge at his memorial, Chaityabhoomi, in Dadar to pay homage. CM's announcement appears to be an outreach to Dalits ahead of the occasion.

A 40-year-old farmer was arrested on Wednesday for allegedly killing his two sons, , aged five and seven, by throwing them into Jayakwadi canal on Monday evening following frequent domestic disputes. The body of the elder son has been recovered from the canal.According to Pachod police in rural Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, accused Somnath alias Parameshwar Rodge (40) took his sons on the scooter on Monday evening on the pretext of buying chocolates, vada pav and taking them for an outing. “He allegedly threw both of them into the canal. Farmers who witnessed the incident tried to intervene, but he allegedly abused them and pelted stones at them,” police said.Pachod police registered a murder FIR against Rodge based on a complaint filed by his wife, Sushma (27) on Wednesday. “A group of farmers spotted Aryan alias Ayush Somnath Rodge around 9am in the Indegaon-Bramhagaon stretch of the canal while heading to switch on water pumps. They pulled the body out and alerted authorities. After a postmortem at the rural hospital in Pachod, the body was handed over to the family,” an officer said.Police said teams from Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar Municipal Corporation fire department, divers and police personnel continued the search operation for five-year-old Shyam.Sub-divisional police officer Sunil Patil said Rodge told investigators that frequent arguments with his wife, Sushma (27), over their children’s upbringing had prompted the crime. “He has confessed that he wanted to kill both the children,” Patil said.Inspector Mahadev Naikwade of Pachod police said the accused also told investigators that he had planned to end his own life and had contemplated killing his wife too, but she had not accompanied him and therefore escaped “a similar fate” as their sons.Ayush’s last rites were performed at Nandar village on Wednesday evening amid tight police security. Police continue to investigate the circumstances leading to the crime.
Article Summary: A 40-year-old farmer was arrested on Wednesday for allegedly killing his two sons, aged five and seven, by throwing them into Jayakwadi canal on Monday evening. The body of the elder son has been recovered from the canal. Pachod police registered a murder FIR against the accused based on a complaint filed by his wife.

Police, however, said preliminary findings pointed to suicide. Further investigations are under way.

Article Title: CJP conducts Lok Sabha seat-wise outreach programme across Maharashtra, focuses on youth mobilisation

Cockroach Janta Party has launched a statewide organisational expansion drive across Maharashtra , stepping up Lok Sabha-level outreach to strengthen its grassroots network, recruit young volunteers, and build campaigns around local public issues such as education, employment, and civic accountability.As part of the four-day exercise led by national organisation in-charge Ajinkya Shinde, party teams toured Satara, Kolhapur, Sangli and Solapur between Nov 14 and 17, holding meetings with youngsters, volunteers and local workers to expand the organisation at the constituency level.The Maharashtra campaign forms part of CJP’s nationwide expansion programme being coordinated by its national working committee through zonal committees across the country.According to a party statement issued on Wednesday, the delegation included West Zone in-charge Kshitij Pagar, joint organisation secretary Akshay Shinde, West Zone coordinator Saroj Shaikh and local coordinators.During the tour, the party convened Lok Sabha-level volunteers’ meetings and outreach sessions in rural areas to gather feedback on local concerns and improve coordination among grassroots workers.“We will build a strong CJP team across Maharashtra that effectively raises the issues of the people. Building a strong organisational force to address the fundamental issues faced by the youth is the need of the hour. I am confident that the newly appointed team will effectively voice public concerns and spearhead the party’s expansion across the state,” Shinde said.The delegation also visited the homes of volunteers who had participated in party protests in Mumbai and Delhi, interacting with them and their parents to explain the party’s vision of building a transparent and accountable democratic movement driven by ordinary citizens.CJP simultaneously launched a membership drive, urging supporters to join Lok Sabha-level teams and participate in civic initiatives. It also began activities under its ‘School Theek Karo’ campaign aimed at highlighting and addressing issues in govt schools.CJP said its expansion strategy centres on establishing active representation from village to Lok Sabha levels, taking up public issues through ground-level interventions and developing young citizens as future leaders of the political movement.
Article Summary: Cockroach Janta Party has launched a statewide organisational expansion drive across Maharashtra. Party teams toured Satara, Kolhapur, Sangli and Solapur between Nov 14 and 17. The Maharashtra campaign forms part of CJP’s nationwide expansion programme.

Article Title: 16-hour firefight brings Harsul waste plant blaze under control
Article Text:
Fire fighters dousing the flames at the Harsul waste processing unit

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar

:

Two machines were damaged and a 15,000sqft dry waste shed was destroyed after a major fire broke out at the Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar Municipal Corporation (CSMC) waste processing unit in Harsul in the early hours of Wednesday.No casualties were reported in the incident, the authorities said. The fire brigade received a call around 4.35 am and dispatched five water tenders, along with several other tankers, to the site.Firefighters brought the blaze and internal combustion under control after nearly 16 hours, with a couple of water tenders kept on standby until night. According to local residents, thick smoke had engulfed the waste processing unit shortly after midnight.Municipal commissioner Amol Yedge, who visited the site, said waste processing had slowed down due to Diwali vacations , leading to a large accumulation of solid waste at the unit. “The heaps of waste helped the fire spread and turned it into a major one, making firefighting difficult,” he said.Yedge said an inquiry had been ordered into the fire incident. CCTV footage from the facility will be examined as part of the inquiry to ascertain how the fire started and whether there was any lapse.While the pre-sorting and baling machines and the shed suffered damage in the fire, Yedge said both the damaged machines were insured, and insurance claims will be made.Chief fire officer Ashok Khandekar said some of the metal sheets of the shed were broken to effectively facilitate firefighting.“Flames were flickering deep inside the smoldering waste heap, while dense white and grey smoke filled the structure and spread across the surrounding locality. Even if the fire was brought under control after 16 hours, we have kept two water tenders on standby to rule out further flare due to possible internal combustion of waste,” he said.The Harsul plant is one of the three main waste processing plants of the CSMC, along with Chikalthana and Padegaon. The fire incident is most likely to adversely impact the daily waste processing in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar to a certain extent.
Article Summary: Two machines were damaged and a 15,000sqft dry waste shed was destroyed. The fire broke out at the Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar Municipal Corporation (CSMC) waste processing unit in Harsul. No casualties were reported in the incident.

Article Title: After YCMOU scam, section of stakeholders demand return to old offline evaluation
Article Text:
YCMOU
