Several teachers, authorised examiners and student representatives have demanded that YCMOU scraps online paper checking and revert to old offline practice, following the irregularities flagged during answer sheet evaluation between June 9 and July 4 this year.About 19,231 answer sheets were allegedly evaluated by unauthorised people who misused biometric thumb impressions of authorised examiners at a college in Lasur Station Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar district. Complainants said the case has exposed the weakness of the online system.The demand has gained ground after Shillegaon police charged 48 people, including a college principal and a CAP centre director on Nov 15 for allegedly claiming Rs2,76,418 as remuneration for the unauthorised evaluation. While the irregularity occurred months ago at the CAP center, YCMOU authorities lodged an FIR only after its internal probes were over.“In the old practice, the examiner had to be physically present at the centre, take delivery of the answer sheet bundle, evaluate them in front of supervisors and return them after signing. There was no way to create a proxy in the examiner’s name,” said a teacher.In the online system, educational activist Tukaram Saraf said, the entire security rests on a biometric login.“Once the thumb impression is captured, the portal opens and anyone can sit on the terminal and evaluate. The physical absence of the authorised examiner becomes impossible to detect any wrongdoing,” he said.Stakeholders also argued that moderation was more effective in the offline system because moderators could see the marks given on answer sheets, the total count and remarks, if any, on papers. In online evaluation, they claimed, work is often hurried to meet targets, and errors go unnoticed till revaluation.“Technology that can be bypassed by a single thumb impression cannot be trusted with lakhs of answer sheets. A foolproof system with live CCTV monitoring, real-time physical verification of examiners and strict login audit is the need of the hour and YCMOU should return to the old practice of physical evaluation at CAP centres,” said Rahul Makasare, a student representative.When contacted, YCMOU spokesperson, Mahendra Bansode said no formal representation has been made so far demanding return to old offline evaluation.
Article Summary: About 19,231 answer sheets were allegedly evaluated by unauthorised people who misused biometric thumb impressions of authorised examiners at a college in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar district. Complainants said the case has exposed the weakness of the online system.

Railway police have booked four employees of a finance company for abetment to suicide after the family of a 57-year-old farmer alleged that relentless loan recovery pressure and threats drove him to end his life.Datta Mohanrao Umate, a marginal farmer from Ganpur village in Nanded ’s Umri taluka, was found dead on railway tracks in the Bolsa area on Nov 15, a day after he left home and failed to return.Based on a complaint filed by his wife, Parvatibai Umate, Govt Railway Police in Nanded registered a case against four finance company employees.“We have registered a case of abetment to suicide against four finance company employees. Further investigation is underway to establish the circumstances leading to Umate’s death and verify the allegations against the employees,” said inspector Prakash Waghmare.According to the family, Umate had borrowed Rs 1.5 lakh from the finance company’s Nanded branch in 2018 to build a house. While he had regularly repaid instalments, about Rs 1 lakh remained outstanding.Parvatibai and her son, Shankar, alleged that recovery agents repeatedly visited their house, demanded immediate repayment and threatened to seal the property if the dues were not cleared.Matters escalated on Oct 17 when a confrontation allegedly broke out between the recovery agents and Umate’s family. The finance company employees subsequently lodged a complaint at Umri police station, following which a case was registered against Umate and his family members.The family alleged that the visits and pressure continued even after the police complaint, pushing the farmer into severe mental distress. Umate left home on Nov 14 and went missing. His body was found on railway tracks the next morning. Railway police recovered the body and launched an investigation.The case has renewed scrutiny of loan recovery practices in the state. It comes weeks after another controversy involving farmer Chandrakant Shinde, who was allegedly assaulted and detained by finance company employees over loan recovery before being found dead under suspicious circumstances. The incident had triggered public outrage and police action.
Article Summary: Datta Mohanrao Umate, a marginal farmer from Ganpur village in Nanded ’s Umri taluka, was found dead on railway tracks on Nov 15. His family alleged that relentless loan recovery pressure and threats drove him to end his life. The case has renewed scrutiny of loan recovery practices in the state.

The Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar district administration has ordered action against colleges and principals allegedly collecting examination fees from students despite a fee waiver announced by Dr Babasaheb Ambedkar Marathwada University (Bamu).In a recent letter to BAMU, resident deputy collector Janardhan Vidhate directed the university to take immediate action against such colleges in accordance with state govt rules.The order came after Rahul Makasare, leader of the Vanchit Bahujan Yuva Aghadi, submitted a representation alleging that several colleges and principals were still collecting exam fees from students.“Colleges that collected exam fees should be ordered to immediately refund the amount. Also, exam fees paid by the wards of distressed farmers should be refunded on a priority basis,” he said.Bamu administration said students who had already paid examination fees despite the state govt’s drought-related waiver will now get their money back from their colleges, with the varsity having already handed over the refund cheques.“We directed 34 colleges to immediately refund students after they took back cheques totalling Rs 1,36,44,756 on Nov 6 and 7,” Bamu’s examinations and evaluation board director B N Dole said.“The university kept its examination department open during the Diwali holidays to facilitate the process. Article Title: 335 CCTV cameras, 4,656 police personnel deployed for Kartiki Ekadashi
Article Text:
The arrangements include 335 CCTV cameras, watchtowers, special anti-theft squads and dedicated police help centres across the pilgrimage town

Kolhapur:

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Traffic diversions and parking arrangements





Elaborate security arrangements have been put in place in Pandharpur to ensure safety of Warkaris and devotees during Kartiki Ekadashi Yatra. A total of 4,656 police personnel have been deployed to manage security, regulate crowd movement and ensure smooth traffic flow. The arrangements include 335 CCTV cameras, watchtowers, special anti-theft squads and dedicated police help centres across the pilgrimage town.Additional superintendent of police Prerna Katte said, “The safety of devotees is the administration’s top priority. Watchtowers have been erected at major crowded locations, including the riverbanks, 65-acre area, Mahadwar area, Mahadwar Ghat and Patrashed, to monitor crowd movement and enable prompt action in case of congestion. A special ‘Mauli squad’ has been formed to prevent thefts and pickpocketing. Around 335 CCTV cameras have been installed at important locations across the city. Seven pilgrimage police help centres have also been established at key locations, including Savarkar Chowk, Shivaji Chowk, Chandrabhaga riverbank and Ambabai Patangan.”Security deployment comprises one superintendent of Police, one additional superintendent of police, 18 deputy superintendents of police, 46 police inspectors and 278 assistant police inspectors and police sub-inspectors.In addition, 2,522 police personnel, 100 Gamma Squad personnel and 1,620 home guards have been deployed.The arrangements also include three State Reserve Police Force (SRPF) teams, two bomb detection and disposal squads, two Quick Action Squads, Quick Response Teams (QRTs) and nine trained CART squads.Meanwhile, district collector S. Karthikeyan has ordered a one-way traffic arrangement on Paschim Dwar-to-Chauphala route from 6 am on Nov 20 to 11.59 am on Nov 21 to prevent congestion and ensure the safe movement of devotees during Kartiki Ekadashi.Lakhs of devotees are expected to visit Chandrabhaga river for a holy dip before proceeding for darshan of Shri Vitthal-Rukmini. Mahadwar Ghat and its surrounding areas are particularly vulnerable to heavy congestion during the pilgrimage.The administration has decided to regulate the movement of devotees with the help of human chains and ropes. As Shri Vitthal-Rukmini temple area has limited access routes, the risk of congestion and accidents increases during peak hours.The one-way arrangement is expected to facilitate the movement of Warkaris towards Chauphala, reduce overcrowding and ensure safer passage for pilgrims.Heavy vehicles have been diverted away from the city, while 13 traffic diversion points have been established to ensure smooth traffic flow. Parking facilities for private vehicles have been arranged at 13 locations inside and outside the city.The police have appealed to pilgrims to remain alert in crowded areas, take care of their valuables, follow traffic regulations and cooperate with the police by adhering to their instructions.
Article Summary: A total of 4,656 police personnel have been deployed to manage security, regulate crowd movement and ensure smooth traffic flow. The arrangements include 335 CCTV cameras, watchtowers, special anti-theft squads and dedicated police help centres across the pilgrimage town.

Tension gripped the Nirman Chowk area of Kolhapur after a 19-year-old youth was attacked on Monday evening following a dispute rooted in past enmity.In retaliation, a mob of 10 people allegedly attacked the house of one of the suspects and vandalised 10 vehicles — including two-wheelers, cars and an autorickshaw — in the area late on Tuesday.The stone-pelting triggered panic among residents. The Juna Rajwada police subsequently registered cases against members of both groups and detained five people in connection with the incidents.Based on a complaint filed by the injured, identified as Vaibhav Kamble, a resident of Rajaram Chowk in the Timber Market area, the police registered a case against four accused.Kamble and one of the accused were friends, but he had been involved in a dispute with one of the accused in 2024.The accused allegedly chased Kamble on a motorcycle on Monday evening and intercepted him near Juna Vashi Naka. They abused him and assaulted him with kicks and sticks. During the attack, one of the accused allegedly struck Kamble on the head with a stick, leaving him critically injured.Following the attack, tensions escalated in the area. According to a complaint lodged by Ajay Shashikant Sutar (25), a resident of Mailkhadda near Nirman Chowk, the police registered another case against 10 people.Inspector Kiran Londhe, while talking to, said, “We have detained five people from both groups. Search for others is underway. Further investigation is ongoing.”
